$comment: Machine-readable twin of PARITY-MATRIX.md. A CI check (docs/parity/check_parity.py, run by the `contracts` job in .github/workflows/sdk-verify.yml) asserts every ABSENT/PARTIAL row has an owning phase and a named E2E flow and that every row cites evidence, so the roadmap cannot rot silently.
$reauditNote: Every row re-read against main. Line numbers in `evidence` had drifted across most rows and are refreshed here. Three states changed: P21 PARTIAL->PRESENT (the evaluation budget and its 504 shipped), P10 PRESENT->PARTIAL and P17 PRESENT->PARTIAL (both were scored on implementing code alone; neither has a test covering the thing the row actually claims). P22's palette gap is closed and its clause deleted.
source: changelog of a larger decisioning platform, assessed against rulemind-ai @ main

features.name: Datasource management + connection testing
features.evidence: app/connector_fetch.py retrieves a source at decision time, opt-in per connector (config.fetch_at_decision). request_mapping composes the outbound call through templates.resolve_template -- the same templating an action step's url/headers/body use -- and response_mapping reshapes the reply through jsonpath.resolve_jsonpath, the resolver rule conditions already use; neither had a single backend reader before. Transport goes through egress.build_pinned_request (DNS + private-range check, connection pinned to the vetted IP, follow_redirects=False) and reuses connector_probe's URL, auth, classification and redaction helpers so "test connection" and decision time cannot diverge. Retrieval runs in executor._fetch_sources BEFORE variables are computed, because steps run after them. Tenant- and connector-scoped response cache with a clamped TTL; per-attempt timeouts and name resolution both clamped to the remaining evaluation budget and resolution moved off the event loop. Covered by tests/test_connector_fetch.py (46) and tests/test_connector_fetch_refuted.py (29).
features.gap: The fast path (FAST_DECIDE=1) DECLINES rather than implements: fast_decide.fast_path_eligible returns False for any tenant with a fetch-configured connector, so those decisions take the full executor. Deliberate -- fast_decide is sync and called from a threadpool, so a second async transport, cache and fail-closed policy there would be the divergence the decline avoids -- but it does mean fetch and the fast path are mutually exclusive.
features.e2eFlow: author a connector -> test the connection -> use it in a workflow
features.note: PARTIAL -> PRESENT 2026-09-05. The old gap -- "connectors never FETCH" -- is closed, and the fail-open behind it with it: _execute_connector used to answer a source it had never contacted with that connector's sample_payload, which is by construction a healthy approving example, at {"status": "ok"}. Nothing here answers a failed fetch with sample data; the default on failure is review_gate, and an unrecognised on_fetch_failure falls back to the safe value rather than to continue. Three adversarial reviews refuted the first implementation and all three were right -- a connector step nested in a branch or sub-workflow was never fetched and still got sample data, an unmapped empty 200 counted as success, and name resolution sat outside the budget (4013ms measured against a 300ms budget) while blocking the event loop. Those fixes and their tests are in tests/test_connector_fetch_refuted.py.

features.name: p12 / PKCS#12 datasource credentials
features.evidence: app/client_certs.py presents a client certificate on outbound calls, from a PKCS#12 bundle stored on the connector (config.client_cert_p12 + client_cert_passphrase). PKCS#12 rather than a PEM pair because that is what a partner's onboarding pack contains -- one password-protected file holding key, leaf and chain -- and splitting it with openssl first means an operator handling a private key by hand. Wired into connector_fetch._build_request, so the identity rides on the request and reaches httpx as `verify`; server verification is NOT weakened (the context starts from ssl.create_default_context, and there is a test asserting check_hostname and CERT_REQUIRED). Intermediates from the bundle are included, or a partner without the chain cached rejects the handshake with an error that looks like a bad certificate rather than a missing one. Contexts are cached per (tenant, connector, bundle fingerprint): the fingerprint is in the key so a rotation takes effect without a restart, and the tenant is in it because connector ids are seeded identically per tenant. tests/test_client_certs.py (23).
features.e2eFlow: upload a client cert -> connector calls a mutually-authenticated endpoint
features.gap: The bundle is configured through the connector's config rather than through a dedicated upload endpoint with its own RBAC, and there is no expiry warning -- a certificate that lapses surfaces as a handshake failure at decision time rather than as a notice beforehand. mtls.evaluate_client_cert already computes expiry for the inbound direction and is the piece to reuse.
features.note: ABSENT -> PRESENT 2026-09-05. The old gap was '0 hits for p12/PKCS12/.pfx; app/mtls.py:128 is INBOUND client-cert verification' -- correct, and this is the opposite direction. Python's ssl module cannot build a client identity from memory (load_cert_chain reads paths only), so the decrypted PEM touches a 0600 temp file that is unlinked immediately after load and in a `finally`; the key then lives only in the SSLContext. Two of the seven mutations run against this were exactly that leak, and both are caught.

features.name: Outbound webhooks with event-type filters
features.evidence: A first-class subscription entity: `webhook_subscriptions` table (migration 20260905_0025), CRUD at /api/v1/webhook-subscriptions plus a /test endpoint (app/routers/webhook_subscriptions.py), and delivery in app/webhook_dispatch.py. EVENT TYPES are a closed list of 13 (the audit event types the backend already emits, plus the decision lifecycle) so a typo is refused at authoring time rather than stored as a subscription that silently never fires. FILTERS are ANDed {path, operator, value} conditions evaluated through logic.compare -- the operator set the five engines are held to -- and a filter that cannot be evaluated does NOT deliver, because over-delivery of decision data to a third party is the worse failure. Deliveries are HMAC-signed with auth.hmac_signature, the same helper webhooks.py VERIFIES inbound, over the exact bytes sent. Transport goes through egress.build_pinned_request with follow_redirects=False. Covered by tests/test_webhook_dispatch.py (32) and tests/test_webhook_subscriptions_api.py (23), and probed -- not exempted -- in tests/test_tenant_isolation_matrix.py. EMISSION is wired, which is what the e2eFlow actually asks for: storage exposes an audit-listener registry (register_audit_listener) and webhook_dispatch.on_audit_event is registered at startup, so the ten event types that flow through add_audit_event are subscribable without a per-call-site hook. Delivery is fire-and-forget on a daemon thread -- a subscriber is not a dependency of the thing that emitted the event and must not delay or fail it -- and per-subscription delivery health (last_delivery_ok, consecutive_failures) makes a silently failing receiver visible. Decisions emit too, hooked at storage.add_decision -- the documented single place a Decision row is written, and therefore the one hook that cannot miss either the fast path or the executor path. decision.completed fires for every outcome, with decision.rejected / decision.review_required alongside so the common case needs no filter; the applicant payload is deliberately NOT shipped, since a subscription is a standing feed to a third party. tests/test_webhook_emission_e2e.py (20) drives the row's stated flow end to end -- subscribe to decision.rejected with a filter, run a decision, verify the signed payload at a stub receiver -- plus a cross-tenant negative on the DELIVERY path and a wall-clock assertion that a slow subscriber cannot delay the emitter.
features.gap: No durable outbox: a subscriber down for the whole retry window misses that event. The decision and the audit write are unaffected either way -- delivery is deliberately best-effort for the emitter, which is the opposite polarity from connector_fetch and for the opposite reason (a decision NEEDS a connector's answer and merely ANNOUNCES to a subscriber). The decision-WAL dead letter added in the same cycle is the pattern to reuse when durability is wanted.
features.e2eFlow: subscribe to decision.rejected with a filter -> run a policy -> signed payload reaches a stub receiver
features.note: PARTIAL -> PRESENT 2026-09-05. The old gap was 'no subscription model, no event types, no filters' -- all three now exist. Routes require manage_access, not author: a policy_maker can already POST anywhere from an action step, so this is not about reaching the network; a subscription is standing egress configuration that sends workspace decision data to a third party until removed, which belongs with settings and branding.

features.name: Workflow step-through debugger
features.evidence: only post-hoc traces (ctx.trace), plus a loop-only debugger: app/executor.py:794 debug_loop returns a per-iteration trace without persisting a decision, exposed at app/routers/runtime.py:334-335 and tested in tests/test_workflow_loops.py:55; /api/v1/executions/{id} and /resume now live at app/routers/sdk.py:353,340; 0 hits for breakpoint/step_through/step_into as product features
features.e2eFlow: open a failing execution -> step through it -> inspect per-step state
features.note: Re-audit 2026-09-04 dropped 'already exist but are untested' -- the /sdk/v1 twins are covered by tests/test_sdk_runtime.py:177,232,333 and the /api/v1 resume by tests/test_rbac_and_tenant_failclosed.py:75. Still ABSENT: replay and a loop tracer are not step-through.
features.gap: No step-through: there is no way to pause a run at a step, inspect the context as it stood there, and advance one step. `ctx.trace` is post-hoc (what already happened) and `debug_loop` re-evaluates a single loop step in isolation — neither lets an operator walk a failing execution. Needs a paused-execution surface the UI can drive, and it is the phase-5 item the roadmap flags as having zero test coverage today.

features.name: Nested-key input validation
features.evidence: Nested-key input validation: app/input_schema.py validates the decision payload against what connectors already declare (schema_paths for required nested paths, sample_payload for types), reporting every issue at once with its full path including array indices. Hooked into app/executor.py before any variable computes, so an invalid payload produces no outcome, no Decision row and no billable unit. Gated by engine_config.input_validation (off|warn|enforce, default off); an unreadable mode resolves to enforce. Covered by apps/python-executor/tests/test_nested_input_validation.py (31 tests). Extended 2026-09-05 to the fast path: app/fast_decide.py validates before any variable computes, off the same tenant_catalog entry the executor reads, and raises input_schema.InputValidationError -- the executor's own class -- so /decide answers an identical 422 with FAST_DECIDE on or off. tests/test_fast_path_validation_and_budget_parity.py asserts the two paths return the same issue set, including array indices (bank.salary[1].amount), and that a rejected payload leaves no Decision row on either.
features.gap: The model-predict path (app/routers/models.py) is still flat. core/engine.py's validate_input is also flat, but that is NOT this gap: it validates an unrelated policy["input_schema"], which storage.py only ever persists for model rows (4007/4045/4064) and never onto a policy, and core/engine.py is the no-I/O module shared with the Kotlin, Dart and TS runtimes -- it has no access to connectors or tenant engine_config, which are what the nested schema is derived from.
features.size: days for the remaining model-predict path
features.e2eFlow: submit a nested payload with a missing leaf -> INVALID_INPUT names the path
features.note: Promoted 2026-09-05. The stated e2eFlow -- a nested payload with a missing leaf returns INVALID_INPUT naming the path -- is met on BOTH decision paths and covered by a test that asserts they return the identical issue set. It was PARTIAL because FAST_DECIDE=1 skipped validation entirely, which is the same class of defect as the fail-opens: a performance flag that changed correctness. The residual gap is the model-predict path, which is a different flow from the one this row claims.

features.name: Child workflow by alias
features.evidence: Child workflow by alias: app/executor.py _execute_subworkflow resolves config.alias via engine_config.workflow_aliases, supporting both a flat map and an environment-keyed one selected by the parent's status, so promotion does not rewrite parents. Alias wins over ref_id; an unregistered alias never falls back to a stale id; the cycle guard keys on the RESOLVED policy id so two aliases for one policy are one visit; cross-tenant resolution is structurally impossible since the registry and the lookup are both tenant-scoped. app/main.py accepts an alias-only step. Covered by apps/python-executor/tests/test_workflow_alias.py (16 tests).
features.e2eFlow: reference a sub-workflow by alias -> alias resolves at run time

features.name: DLQ / Kafka / exactly-once
features.evidence: The two halves worth having without a broker are both in place. IDEMPOTENCY: app/idempotency.py with an `idempotency_records` table and a (tenant_id, key) unique constraint, so a redelivery of the same request does not double-log a decision. DEAD LETTER: a decision the WAL cannot re-insert is retried up to DECISION_WAL_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS and then moved to a dead-letter file rather than retried on every boot forever -- never deleted, since a WAL record is a decision that was already returned to a caller and is not in the database. It is counted in recover()'s result, logged at ERROR on EVERY boot (not only when something was also replayed), and requeued on demand by decision_wal.replay_dead_letter, which resets the attempt budget and writes back exactly what still fails. tests/test_decision_wal_dead_letter.py (14).
features.e2eFlow: kill a consumer mid-flight -> message lands in the DLQ -> redelivery does not double-log
features.note: ABSENT -> PARTIAL 2026-09-05. The row bundled three things of very different value and cost; the DLQ and idempotency halves are most of the buyer-visible benefit and needed no broker at all.
features.gap: No broker, so no partition, no consumer group and no offset for exactly-once to be ABOUT: messaging is still Redis pub/sub with a DB-polling fallback (app/decision_bus.py). The dead letter covers the durable decision path (the WAL), not a consumer killed mid-flight on a topic, because there is no topic. That is the 6+ month half of this row and it is deliberately not started.

features.name: Canary deployment with delays
features.evidence: app/champion_challenger.py: explicit champion/challenger roles (identify_roles), a traffic ramp schedule (current_ramp_weight over ramp: [{day, weight}, ...]), guardrail metrics (evaluate_guardrails over minApprovalRate/maxRejectRate/maxAvgLatencyMs/maxApprovalRateDropPct), significance testing (two_proportion_pvalue) and an automated promote/rollback/hold recommendation. Surfaced through app/analytics.py, and it GATES promotion: app/routers/experiments.py refuses to promote a challenger the analysis does not recommend unless forced. The ramp drives live traffic as of 2026-09-05 -- app/experiments.py resolves each variant's current weight from the schedule and gives the champion the remainder -- covered by tests/test_champion_challenger.py and tests/test_canary_ramp_assignment.py (14).
features.e2eFlow: promote at 5% canary -> watch the metric -> auto-rollback on SLO breach
features.gap: Nothing ACTS on a "rollback" recommendation on its own. It blocks a manual promote; no scheduler halts an experiment or reverts traffic when a guardrail breaches, so the auto-rollback half of the e2eFlow still needs a human watching.
features.note: Re-audited 2026-09-05, ABSENT -> PARTIAL, and the audit found a live bug rather than just mis-sizing. current_ramp_weight was called only from analytics.py, so assign_variant used the STATIC weight: a canary configured to ramp 10% -> 25% -> 50% served 10% forever while the dashboard rendered the schedule as though it were in effect. Fixed; see the commit for why ramping the challenger alone changes nothing without the champion taking the remainder.

features.name: Feature factory
features.evidence: 0 hits in any .py/.ts/.tsx (only PLAN.md:332); app/backtest.py and app/analytics.py are the seeds
features.e2eFlow: define a derived feature -> backfill it -> use it in a scorecard
features.gap: No feature factory: 0 hits. Variables are authored one at a time in Python; there is no derived-feature pipeline, no backfill, and no feature store to read from at decision time.

features.name: Monaco / embedded code editor
features.evidence: CodeMirror 6 editor at apps/web/src/v3/editor/PythonCodeEditor.tsx, replacing the plain textarea in apps/web/src/v3/pages/VariablesPage.tsx: Python syntax highlighting themed from the app's own tokens (light and dark), bracket closing, history, indent-with-tab, and RuleMind-AWARE completion built from live page state -- apps/web/src/v3/editor/rulemind-completion.ts offers the selected source's sample_payload keys after `payload.`, the workspace's other variables after `variables.`, and the @variable(source=...) decorator and its three parameters. Covered by test/rulemind-completion.test.ts (19 tests) and end-to-end by e2e/rulemind-v3.spec.ts, which types into the editor and reads back its theme.
features.e2eFlow: edit a Python variable with highlighting and RuleMind-aware completion
features.gap: No inline diagnostics: nothing surfaces a syntax or name error before the variable is run against the sandbox (@codemirror/lint is not wired). The editor is also only on the variables page -- the API console and the other textareas are unchanged.
features.note: CodeMirror 6, not Monaco, and the row's own gap text counted either. The dashboard deploys as a Render STATIC SITE and must be self-contained: @monaco-editor/react loads Monaco from a CDN at runtime by default, and self-hosting it under Next's static export needs bespoke worker plumbing. Monaco is also ~5MB against ~250KB for what is one editor on one page.

features.name: Rate limiting on resource APIs
features.evidence: Per-resource-class rate limiting: app/rate_limit.py classify() maps method+path to decision/read/write/ai/export/admin/unclassified with whole-segment matching, check_request() enforces the class bucket then the tenant aggregate, and request_cost() charges bulk endpoints from Content-Length. app/middleware.py calls check_request(). Pre-auth IP-keyed budgets and login lockout in app/middleware.py (check_pre_auth_rate_limit) cover the unauthenticated surface.

features.name: Superflows
features.evidence: Ships under the name SUB-WORKFLOW. app/executor.py handles a `workflow` step, resolving it by raw ref_id or by a per-tenant alias (_resolve_workflow_alias, registry in engine_config.workflow_aliases), loading the sub-policy scoped to the tenant and running its steps at depth+1, with cycle detection on the RESOLVED id so two aliases for one policy cannot smuggle A->B->A back in. The composing thing is itself a policy, so it carries the whole policy lifecycle: app/routers/policies.py promote_policy (dev/uat/prod) imposes no step-type restriction, and versioning and audit come with it. Exposed as a first-class builder primitive at apps/web/app/workflow-builder/page.tsx ({type: "workflow", label: "Sub-workflow"}). Covered by tests/test_workflow.py, test_workflow_alias.py, test_workflow_engine.py and test_workflow_loops.py.
features.e2eFlow: compose workflows into a superflow with its own lifecycle
features.note: Re-audited 2026-09-05, ABSENT -> PRESENT. The row was scored on a name: zero case-insensitive hits for "superflow". Its stated e2eFlow -- compose workflows into a superflow with its own lifecycle -- is met today. NOT marked CUT: CUT in this file means deliberately not built (P14 SQL editor, which has no underlying datasource). Here the capability ships; only the other platform's word for it is missing. This removed a 3-6 month phase-7 item that did not exist.
